extracted_by: hand, T-0313 — the Democrat read, April 1834
note: Vol. I No. 18, and the whole of it is the Tesseract fallback reading on pages 3 and 4 — eighteen of the issue's thirty-two segmenter columns carry the fallback banner and every one of them is on the two pages that hold the town. THE MONTH'S CENTREPIECE IS HERE: the list of letters remaining in the Post Office at Chicago on 1 April 1834, over J. S. C. Hogan's signature, cut across page 3 columns 3 and 4 and minted here (c001, c002). Neither the sweep in `data/research/newspapers/README.md` nor T-0313's own brief knew of it — both name 1834-04-23 and 1834-04-30 as April's letter lists, and those two are the HENNEPIN list, not Chicago's. The heading survives as `SQA AINIG init`, which is why every keyword sweep for 'list of letters' walked past it. Beside the list: the Board of Trustees' sidewalk ordinance for South Water Street (c003), which is the most placeable thing the month prints, and a block of storefronts placed against Graves' tavern, Newberry & Dole's store and the corners of Water and Clark and of Dearborn and Lake. `locator.lines` is the whole advertisement as the segmenter cut it; `lines_of_claim` is the subset quoted.

claims.notes: THE CENSUS PROXY FOR APRIL 1834 and the reason this issue is the month's biggest unit of work. Ruling 1: a listed name mints a resident candidate, so every name here is an entity and every one carries `letter_list_only`. THE HEADING IS WHY NOBODY HAD FOUND IT: line 2854 reads `E ELECTOR. | SQA AINIG init`, in which `SQA AINIG` is `REMAINING` and the words `List of Letters` are not on the page at all in this column — they stand at line 3018 in the next segmenter column, over the list's second half. Every sweep this project has run for 'list of letters' / 'letters remaining' / 'remaining in the post office' / 'uncalled for' / a signature ending 'P. M.' therefore missed April's Chicago list, and `data/research/newspapers/README.md` says in as many words that only four of T-0258's thirty issues carry one. It is six. THE SEGMENTER INTERLEAVES: each line of this column carries the tail of the editorial from the printed column to its left AND one name from the list, so the quote is the whole cut line and the names are read out of its right-hand half. NORMALIZED AGAINST THE REPRINT: the same list is printed again on 1834-04-08, where this half reads distinctly cleaner, and 04-08's reading is what settles `Robt. V. Allen`, `Ebenezer Alden`, `Maria S. Arnold`, `Thos. W. Bradley`, `Oscar L. Hawley` and `Alexander Fullerton`. That is a corroborating witness resolving an OCR judgement, not a second minting: 04-08's own claims mint only the names THIS printing lost (T-0299). 163 names are minted from the two halves; eleven lines here and eight in column 4 carry debris where a name stood and are left unread rather than guessed at, so 163 is a FLOOR and not the printed length. The gap is T-0319, not an estimate.

claims.notes:
The second half of the same list, and the half that carries the heading `List of Letters` (line 3018) and the postmaster's signature (line 3115). J. S. C. HOGAN is NOT `letter_list_only` in substance — he signs the list rather than being named in it — but the flag is carried by the CLAIM and not the entity, so the compiler marks him `letter_list_only` here and his other mentions in this corpus retire the flag, which is exactly the mechanism ruling 1 asks for. The address line reads `the Post Office a Chi` and `day of peer mea`: the town is legible, the date is not, and it is supplied from the 1834-04-08 reprint, which reads `on the first day` and from the endorsement `April 1, 1834` that stands under the list's second column there. Eight lines of this half — 3039 to 3045 — carry the interleaved editorial where names stood, and the 1834-04-08 reprint shows what was lost there: Isaac Merrill, Chas. Manning, James Mulford, Philo C. Mills and James McKee. They are minted from 04-08 and not from here, because here they are not on the page. THE THIRD PRINTING, FOUND 2026-08-29 (T-0321): this list is printed a THIRD time, at chicago_democrat_1834_04_16 page 4 columns 2 and 3 (c016 and c017 there), and that printing's J-W half is the cleanest witness the corpus holds — one name per line, no debris. It settles the seven lines 3039-3045 as holding the five names 1834-04-08 supplied and nothing else, and it adds eight names this printing lost entirely: Samuel Louis, Gregory E. Legg, P. F. W. Peck, William Power, Mason B. Smith, Robt. Strong, Dr. Trimball, D. V. S. Torry and Elam Tuller, minted there and not here. IT ALSO UNDOES A CONFLATION MADE HERE. This half prints TWO Walkers, at lines 3105 (`« . Walker`) and 3110 (`G. He Walker`); the third printing and the 1834-04-08 reprint both set them as `Geo. E. Walker` between Mansfield Wheeler and Jeddiah Woolley and `G. H. Walker` between Elihu Walter and Tho. C. Webb. Line 3105 was dropped in this reading and line 3110 was normalized as `G[eo]. [E]. Walker` — the second Walker wearing the first one's initials. Line 3110 is corrected to G. H. Walker, which is what its own line reads; Geo. E. Walker is minted from the third printing, where he is legible.

THREE OF THESE LINES ARE READ AT THE PAGE IMAGES (T-1138) and seventy-nine are not, so this claim stays `transcription_mediated`. Entities 58, 59 and 60 carry `read_at_image` and `reading: scan_verified` individually: the advertisement of the next column bleeds through them here, the 16 April impression's extraction read the same three positions differently, and all three impressions of the return were read at the scan to settle it. `data/research/newspapers/letter_list_1834_04_01_contested_lines.json` is the reading, with the IIIF regions each line was read at.

claims.notes: A DWELLING HOUSE PLACED BY SURVEY AND A COURT HOUSE PLACED BY NAME. The levy fixes Saunders's house by quarter-section — the north half of the [—] quarter of the north west quarter of a section in township 40 north, range 14 east — and township 40 is NORTH of the township the town stands in, so this house is outside the plat and is recorded as such. The section number is cut and is not supplied. The second building is the one the case is returnable at: `the court house in the town of Chicago`, 14 May 1834, which is the same court house three suits reported on 1834-04-16 name. `40` is quoted as the transcription gives it and is NOT corrected to 39 to make the house fall inside the town: a wrong township is a different building.
